reference_title: Drilled Shafts: Construction Procedures and LRFD Design Methods

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: Specifications for drilled shaft construction must strike a balance between prescriptive requirements and performance-based criteria. The chapter presents a guide specification framework that can be adapted for project-specific requirements. Good specifications protect the owner by establishing quality standards while allowing the contractor flexibility to use the most efficient construction methods.
key_points: Balance between prescriptive and performance-based requirements
Guide specification framework provided for project adaptation
Specifications should allow contractor flexibility while maintaining quality
Must coordinate with contract drawings and geotechnical report
sections.applicability: Development of drilled shaft construction specifications

sections.title: Approach to Drilled Shaft Specifications
sections.body: The recommended approach uses a performance-based guide specification format with commentary notes to assist specification writers. The specification is organized into standard CSI format sections covering description, materials, construction methods, and quality control. Commentary notes explain the intent of each provision and provide guidance on when modifications may be appropriate for specific project conditions.
key_points: Performance-based specification format recommended over method-based
CSI format organization with commentary notes
Method specifications restrict contractor flexibility and increase cost
Owner should establish performance requirements and allow contractor to determine means and methods
sections.applicability: Specification format and philosophy for drilled shaft contracts

sections.title: Construction Methods
sections.body: Specifications should address the three principal construction methods: dry, cased (temporary and permanent), and wet (slurry or water). The Drilled Shaft Installation Plan submitted by the contractor should describe the proposed methods, equipment, and procedures. A technique shaft (trial installation) may be specified to demonstrate the viability of the proposed methods before production shaft construction begins.
key_points: Three principal methods: dry, cased, and wet (slurry/water)
Contractor submits Drilled Shaft Installation Plan before construction
Technique shaft (trial installation) demonstrates viability of methods
Temporary casing extraction procedures are critical to concrete integrity
Permanent casing specifications include material, dimensions, and grade of steel
sections.applicability: Specifying construction methods for drilled shaft contracts

sections.title: Drilling Fluid
sections.body: Specifications for drilling fluid (slurry) should address the type of slurry (mineral, polymer, or natural), testing requirements, and performance criteria. Key properties include density (unit weight), viscosity (Marsh funnel time), sand content, pH, and filtrate loss. The contractor should submit a Slurry Management Plan. Minimum slurry head above groundwater must be maintained, typically 4 to 6 ft, to ensure stability of the excavation walls.
key_points: Slurry types: mineral (bentonite), polymer, and natural (water-based)
Key properties: density, viscosity, sand content, pH, filtrate loss
Minimum slurry head of 4-6 ft above groundwater for stability
Contractor submits Slurry Management Plan
Sand content must be less than 4% (by volume) before concrete placement
Slurry manufacturer representative should be on-site during initial operations
sections.applicability: Specifying drilling fluid requirements for wet method construction

sections.title: Load Testing
sections.body: Specifications for load testing should reference the applicable ASTM standards and specify the type of test, number of tests, and acceptance criteria. The specification should include provisions for the Drilled Shaft Installation Plan to incorporate load test requirements, instrumentation, and procedures for interpreting results. Both pre-production and proof tests may be specified.
key_points: Reference applicable ASTM standards for each test type
Specify number and location of load tests
Include acceptance criteria and failure definitions
Instrumentation requirements should be clearly stated
sections.applicability: Specifying load test requirements in drilled shaft contracts

sections.title: Integrity Testing
sections.body: Specifications should address post-construction integrity testing methods, primarily crosshole sonic logging (CSL) and gamma-gamma logging (GGL). Provisions should include the number and placement of access tubes, timing of tests relative to concrete placement, acceptance criteria based on velocity reduction or density measurements, and procedures for addressing anomalies. Access tubes should be specified as Schedule 40 steel or PVC with 1.5 to 2-inch inner diameter.
key_points: CSL and GGL are the primary integrity testing methods
One access tube per foot of shaft diameter (minimum two)
CSL testing typically performed 3-7 days after concrete placement
Acceptance criteria based on velocity reduction and energy reduction
Provisions for additional testing when anomalies are detected
sections.applicability: Specifying non-destructive integrity testing for drilled shafts

sections.title: Construction Phase Subsurface Investigations
sections.body: Specifications should allow for additional subsurface investigation during construction when unanticipated conditions are encountered. This may include additional borings, in-situ testing, or evaluation of excavated materials. The specification should include provisions for differing site conditions and procedures for resolving discrepancies between design assumptions and actual conditions.
key_points: Additional investigation may be needed during construction
Provisions for differing site condition procedures
Inspector should compare excavated materials to boring logs
Core hole requirements at base of rock sockets

sections.title: Drilled Shaft Installation Plan
sections.body: The Drilled Shaft Installation Plan is a key contractor submittal that describes the proposed methods, equipment, procedures, and quality control measures for drilled shaft construction. It should include details on excavation equipment, drilling methods, casing type and dimensions, concrete mix design, placement method, reinforcement installation, and slurry management. The plan must be reviewed and approved before the start of construction.
key_points: Contractor submits plan before construction begins
Includes equipment, methods, concrete mix, slurry plan, and QC procedures
Must be approved by the engineer before construction
Updates required when methods or conditions change
Technique shaft results may require revisions to the plan
sections.applicability: Contractor submittal requirements for drilled shaft construction

sections.title: Measurement and Payment
sections.body: Measurement and payment provisions define how the contractor will be compensated for drilled shaft work. Common pay items include drilled shaft excavation (per linear foot by diameter), permanent casing, reinforcing steel, concrete, obstruction removal, and load testing. The specification should define how quantities are measured, what is included in each pay item, and how changes in shaft dimensions or depths are handled.
key_points: Common pay items: excavation (per linear ft), casing, steel, concrete, testing
Excavation typically paid per linear foot by shaft diameter
Separate pay items for obstructions, unanticipated rock, and additional length
Load testing and integrity testing typically separate pay items
Clear definitions prevent disputes during construction
sections.applicability: Contract payment provisions for drilled shaft construction

sections.title: Summary
sections.body: Good specifications are essential for successful drilled shaft construction. The guide specification provided in this chapter offers a comprehensive framework that can be adapted for project-specific requirements. Performance-based specifications that allow contractor flexibility while maintaining quality standards are recommended over prescriptive method specifications.
key_points: Performance-based specifications are preferred over method specifications
Guide specification provides adaptable framework
Coordination between specifications, drawings, and geotechnical report is essential
sections.applicability: Summary guidance for drilled shaft specifications
